name: William Law
role: Counselor in the First Presidency who became a leading dissenter
dateNote: Section 124 named him a counselor in January 1841, and he was excommunicated on 18 April 1844.
importance: Section 124 names him to the First Presidency, tells him to invest in the Nauvoo House, and promises him spiritual gifts if he stays humble. By 1844 he opposed Joseph Smith over the secret practice of plural marriage and other matters. He formed a rival church and published the Nauvoo Expositor in June 1844. The city council ordered the press destroyed, and the resulting charges took Joseph Smith to Carthage.
connections: He served with Joseph Smith, Hyrum Smith, and Sidney Rigdon. Law said Joseph had approached his wife, Jane, a claim Joseph’s supporters denied.
reviewNote: Birth (8 September 1809, County Tyrone, Ireland), presidency service, excommunication, Expositor, and death (January 1892, Shullsburg, Wisconsin) checked on JSP; reasons for his break and the Expositor sequence from Wikipedia. The claim about Jane Law is reported as his claim. Bare “William” in 124:87–102 is not linked.
